title: fix(mcp): validate_expression gives the publish gate's verdict at validation and formula sites
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao6bxPjjxx5Q76zwSbAq6zBX)_

Fixes #32872

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the MCP `validate_expression` tool now answers `ok: false` (or a warning) at a `validation` or `formula` site for an expression the publish gate already refuses (or warns on). The gate's acceptance set does not change, and no existing exported type or signature changes.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the published skills (`objectstack-formula`, `objectstack-ai`) say only that the tool runs the build's validator, which stays true; what it refuses is taught by the served `SKILL.md` line this diff corrects.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:MCP `validate_expression` 在 `validation` / `formula` 位点除共享校验器外,还跑发布门禁自己的那几道检查(经 lint 新导出的 `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression`,对调用者被服务的对象定义跑门禁本身的遍历),门禁拒的它也拒;跳转目标与 `describe_object` 守同一道系统对象围栏;lint 在首次需要时才懒加载;服务端 `SKILL.md` 与 Console 镜像同步改那一行。`flow_condition` 位点不在本 PR(席位另开卡)。
- 为什么改:工具承诺"给出发布门禁对这条规则的判定",却只跑共享校验器,对空值未守卫、跳到目标对象未声明字段、跳进存储元数据表、校验规则读 `parent` 这几类答 `ok: true`,到发布时才第一次被拒。
- 风险与回滚:只收窄一个建议性工具的判定,门禁的接受集不变;门禁接受的表达式答案与之前逐字相同。`@objectstack/mcp` 把 `@objectstack/lint` 从 devDependency 挪到 dependency(无环)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts`(入口:构造门禁要判的 stack 再跑门禁自己的 walk)与 `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` 新增的 `sharedValidatorRunByCaller`(仅跳过共享校验器那一次调用)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/authored-site-expression.test.ts` 与 `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-validate-expression.test.ts`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

This closes #32872 at the two sites the card names, `validation` and `formula`. The gate's own passes at a `flow_condition` (the unprovisioned-anchor warning on an object-bound flow predicate, and the null-guard gate on a record-triggered flow's start, `decision` and edge conditions) are not run by the tool, and this PR does not change its verdict there. They are a follow-up card.

The tool promises the verdict the publish gate gives the rule, but it ran the shared expression validator (`@objectstack/formula`'s `validateExpression`) and nothing else. Measured on `origin/main` before the change, it answered `ok: true` at these sites for rules the gate refuses:

| site | expression (fixture) | gate verdict | tool before | tool after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| both | `record.balance.nope` (hop to a field the target does not declare) | error | ok | error, gate's sentence |
| both | a hop into a stored-metadata table | error | ok | error, gate's sentence |
| `validation` | `record.days > 3`, `days` neither required nor defaulted (null guard) | error | ok | error, gate's sentence |
| `validation` | a read of `parent` | error | ok | error, gate's sentence |
| both | `record.owner_id` on an ADR-0015 `external` object | warning | none | warning, gate's sentence |

- `@objectstack/lint`
  - New `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` (`packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts`). ⛔ It re-implements no pass. It builds the stack the gate would judge (the subject object carrying the one probe rule or probe formula field, plus the hop targets it reads through) and runs the gate's own walk `runStackExpressionPasses` over it, as the object save door does (`runtimeWriteType: 'object'`). It returns exactly the findings the gate locates on that rule or field: by key path `objects[0].validations[0].` at a validation site, and by the field's `where` at a formula site. Any pass later added to the gate at either site is carried by construction.
  - New `authoredExpressionHopTargets`: the reference targets the expression reads through, read with the analysis and target accessor the gate's hop passes use.
  - The gate gains one option, `sharedValidatorRunByCaller`, which skips only the `validateExpression` call the caller has already made. Every other pass runs unchanged. **No gate caller passes it.** Its one passer is the new entry, and a source pin in `authored-site-expression.test.ts` now holds that by test (grep at `8a5f028f`):

    ```
    $ grep -rn "sharedValidatorRunByCaller" packages scripts ui apps   (excluding node_modules, dist)
    packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:2277:  sharedValidatorRunByCaller?: boolean;
    packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:2281: * [#32872] What {@link StackExpressionOptions.sharedValidatorRunByCaller}
    packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:2324:  // [#32872] See {@link StackExpressionOptions.sharedValidatorRunByCaller}.
    packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:2325:  const validatorRunByCaller = options.sharedValidatorRunByCaller === true;
    packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts:22: * already made left out (`sharedValidatorRunByCaller`). What comes back is
    packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts:131:    { runtimeWriteType: 'object', sharedValidatorRunByCaller: true },

    $ grep -rn "runStackExpressionPasses(" packages apps   (excluding node_modules, dist, tests)
    packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:2295:  return runStackExpressionPasses(stack, {});
    packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:827:      runStackExpressionPasses(stack, { runtimeWriteType: ctx.runtimeWriteType }).map((i) => ({
    packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts:129:  const issues = runStackExpressionPasses(
    ```
  - Served definitions carry the system columns the registry injects as declared fields. The gate judges the body as authored, so the entry reads each one through `stripInjectedSystemColumns` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`, the write path's own strip). Without it, the null guard would refuse `created_at`, and an external object's anchors would read as columns its author vouches for.
- `@objectstack/mcp`
  - `McpDataBridge` gains the optional `servedObjectDefinitionOf(name)`: the object definition as the caller is served it (the read `describeObject` projects). It is handed to the gate and rendered to nobody. A bridge without it answers the shared validator's verdict alone, as before. The stdio bridge serves it from its served view.
  - `validate_expression` at `formula` and `validation` merges the gate's findings into `errors` / `warnings`, as `{ source, message }` in the gate's words at the gate's severity. A `flow_condition` and a `template` are not judged by this change, and no definition is read for them.
  - Hop targets follow the same system-object fence as `describe_object`: a target the tool's object-name guard refuses is neither read nor judged, so a hop into a system object is judged only where the server sets `allowSystemObjects`.
  - The tool description and the served `SKILL.md` line name what the tool now refuses, give the unprovisioned-column warning its two sites, and state the fence.
  - **New runtime dependency:** `@objectstack/lint` moves from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` (`packages/mcp/package.json`, with the matching six-line `pnpm-lock.yaml` move). **No cycle:** `@objectstack/lint` depends only on `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/sdui-parser` and `@objectstack/spec`, and none of those depends on `@objectstack/mcp`. `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/cli` already depend on `@objectstack/lint` at runtime. **Loaded lazily:** `gatePassFindings` imports lint's root entry with `await import('@objectstack/lint')` on the first call that judges a rule or formula field, and the module imports only its types, so the boot path still reaches lint only through `@objectstack/lint/runtime`, as every other server-side consumer does. The full workspace build orders it cleanly (119/119 tasks).
- `@objectstack/runtime`: the HTTP MCP bridge serves `servedObjectDefinitionOf` through `readObjectForCaller`, the same caller-scoped read `describeObject` uses (ADR-0106 D1), so a field masked from the caller is masked from the gate's input too.
- `@object-ui/console`: the downloadable `SKILL.md` mirror carries the same line, byte for byte.
- Changeset `.changeset/32872-validate-expression-gate-parity.md`: patch for the four packages, with the **BREAKING** verdict-narrowing banner and an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition. Every expression the tool now refuses, the gate already refused, so neither stored metadata nor consumer code has anything to rewrite.
- Registration only: `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` (the `@objectstack/lint` entry) and `turbo.json` (`@objectstack/lint#test` inputs) declare `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` and its `.d.mts`, which the new lint test imports to read the gate's source without its comments.

## Tests

- `packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.test.ts` (new, 26 tests)
  - **Enumeration pins.** The test reads the gate's source through the shared comment mask.
    - Per site, inside the gate's regions for it (`check` plus the validation-rule loop for `validation`; `judgeFieldFormula` plus the span after its call site for `formula`), every call by bare name is classified as `validator`, `plumbing`, `pass` (with a refusal fixture) or `pass-silent-here`, and every member call by its method name is classified as plumbing.
    - Across the whole walk (`runStackExpressionPasses`), every pass handed to the walk as `issues.push(fn(` or `issues.push(...fn(`, member names included, is classified. That is the shape of the walk's whole-stack passes at its tail (`bulkConfirmTextIssues`, `actionCopyTemplateIssues`).
    - `formulaCycleIssues` (from main) is classified `pass-silent-here` at the formula site, with a pin that it fires on the object's own cycle and locates nothing on the probe.
    - Each addition reds until it is classified. Proven by ablation: a new bare call inside `judgeFieldFormula`, a `formulaCycleIssues`-shaped spread after the fields loop, a new member call there, and a new `issues.push(...)` beside `bulkConfirmTextIssues`.
    - **What it cannot see** (also in the test's docblock): a pass outside the regions that pushes by another shape (an inline `issues.push({ … })`, a loop over a helper's result, a helper that pushes into `issues` itself), and a pass handed by reference (`.map(fn)`). Such a pass is still carried by construction when it locates its finding on the judged rule's key path or the judged field's `where`. What no pin catches is a pass located elsewhere, or one that needs an input the tool is not handed.
  - **The skip option reaches no gate run.** A source scan over lint's own sources (tests aside, comments and literals masked) holds `sharedValidatorRunByCaller` to its declaration, the walk's one read, and the one passer in `authored-site-expression.ts`. A second scan holds `runStackExpressionPasses` and `StackExpressionOptions` off all three package entries.
  - **One refusal pin per pass.** For each pass, the entry's findings equal the gate's own findings on the same stack (the full `runStackExpressionPasses` minus the shared validator's).
  - **CONTROLs.** An accepted rule and an accepted formula answer `[]`.
  - Also: the validator is left to the caller; the subject's own rules are ignored; a served definition (with injected columns) judges as authored; an absent object answers `[]`; hop-target reads.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-validate-expression.test.ts`: a new describe block with one tool-level pin per member (8). It also pins that an injected `created_at` is not refused, that only hop targets are read, a CONTROL equal to the definition-less bridge, that a bridge without the member answers as before, and that `flow_condition` / `template` read no definition. **Fence pin:** a hop into a served `sys_user` is refused with `allowSystemObjects` on. By default the target is not read, and the answer equals the definition-less bridge's.
- The two bridge-member ledgers (`mcp-write-response-internal-fields.tripwire.test.ts`, `stdio-data-bridge.stored-metadata-body.test.ts`) classify the new member. Both went red without the entry, as their ledgers intend.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts` adds `servedObjectDefinitionOf` to the ADR-0106 case table, with a masked field-set assertion. `mcp-option-fields-read.test.ts` pins that it equals the served object, that its keys equal `describeObject`'s fields, and that it answers null when the object is absent.

## Acceptance notes

- **Findings carry no `code`.** The gate's `ExprIssue` has none, so the tool's added findings are `{ source, message }` with the gate's sentence.
- **The probe rule is named `this rule`.** The tool is handed the condition, not the rule it will sit on, so a gate sentence that names the rule (the null guard, `parent`) names it `this rule`. The probe formula field is spelled `__validate_expression__`, and no gate sentence at the formula site names it.
- **The formula-cycle pass (#33108) is classified `pass-silent-here` at the formula site.** It landed on main and this branch merged it. Its call sits after the fields loop, inside the formula region, and both the formula enumeration pin and the whole-walk push pin went red on the merge (`+ "formulaCycleIssues"`) until it was classified. It locates each finding on a cycle member's own `expression`. The probe is named `__validate_expression__`, which no authored formula can read, so the probe is never on a cycle. A pin shows the pass does fire on the object's own cycle, and that neither the gate nor the entry locates a finding on the probe. **Limitation:** the tool cannot give the cycle verdict for the formula being authored, because it is not handed that field's own name. That belongs with the follow-up card.
- **`storedExpressionInputIssues` is `pass-silent-here`.** That holds for a `formula` probe. A stored (non-`formula`) field's `expression` authored through `site: 'formula'` gets the gate's stored-input warnings and none from the tool. This goes with the follow-up card.
- **Context the one-object probe stack does not share with the gate.** These are corners, written down. Only the first two are cases where the tool refuses and the gate does not.
  - Package closure: the object save door narrows `objects` to the written package's closure, so a target outside it is not judged there. The tool judges any target the caller is served. The tool's refusal is true (the field does not exist), and the door's silence is the gap.
  - A target field masked from the caller is refused as undeclared. This conforms to ADR-0106 D1 and to what the shared validator already answers for a masked subject field.
  - A target the caller is not served, or a system-object target behind the fence, is not judged, so the tool stays `ok` where the gate refuses. This residual runs in the pre-existing direction.
  - A picklist-bound field is served with resolved `options`. A default option makes it non-nullable for the tool, while the authored body the gate reads names only the picklist.
  - The entry finds the subject by `name === objectName`. On the bridge's no-protocol fallback, a differently spelled name answers `[]`.
  - A fault-tier target turns the call into a door error instead of a verdict, the same answer `describe_object` gives for that target.
- **Scope of the hint lists.** The tool's `fields` / stdlib hints still come from the tool's own index. Only the verdict reads the gate.
- **The shared validator runs once.** The tool keeps its own `validateExpression` call, which carries `code`s and the site options. The gate's copy is skipped, so a validator finding is never reported twice.

1 null-guard (formula) | formula | `record.days > 3 ? 1 : 0` | gate: none | tool ok=true, errors=0, warnings=0
2 undeclared hop | validation | `record.balance.nope > 1` | gate: error: | tool ok=true, errors=0, warnings=0

3 stored body hop | validation | `record.meta.name == 'x'` | gate: error: | tool ok=true, errors=0, warnings=0
3 stored body hop | formula | `record.meta.name == 'x' ? 1 : 0` | gate: error: | tool ok=true, errors=0, warnings=0
3 parent root | validation | `parent.remaining > 1` | gate: error: | tool ok=true, errors=0, warnings=0
3 parent root (formula) | formula | `parent.remaining > 1 ? 1 : 0` | gate: none | tool ok=true, errors=0, warnings=0

The formula rows for the null guard and `parent` show no gate finding: the gate runs those two passes only at a validation rule, and the entry follows it.
